summary: Verified both new features end-to-end. (1) Expanded squads: /api/players?current_club_id=<id> returns Real Madrid 20 players (sum 1250.0 Mio €), Manchester City 18 players (sum 1003.0 Mio €), Bayern München 43 players (657.5 Mio €). Club pages render Kader tab with all players, sidebar shows Kaderwert = 1250.0 / 1003.0 / 657.5 Mio € respectively. (2) Transfer linking: /api/players/{id}/transfers now returns from_club_slug and to_club_slug on each transfer row. Frontend TransferRow renders both club names as <a href='/verein/<slug>'> anchors. On Messi's Transfers tab, links found: Paris Saint-Germain -> /verein/paris-saint-germain, Inter Miami -> /verein/inter-miami, FC Barcelona -> /verein/fc-barcelona. On Haaland's tab: Manchester City -> /verein/manchester-city, Borussia Dortmund -> /verein/borussia-dortmund. Clicking PSG link navigates correctly to /verein/paris-saint-germain (verified page.url).

issues: Bayern has 43 seeded players but only ~7 have market_value populated; Kaderwert of 657.5 Mio € reflects only players with values. Consider showing '(x/y Spieler mit Marktwert)' for transparency.

critical_code_review_comments: Transfer response now includes from_club_slug/to_club_slug — good. Ensure DB constraint or backfill script exists so future transfers always include slugs; otherwise TransferRow will silently degrade to plain text.
GET /api/transfers?player_id=<id> returns 500 (see internal error); only /api/players/{id}/transfers works. Consider removing the broken query variant or fixing it for API consistency.
Kaderwert is client-side summed from player.market_value; players without market_value silently reduce the total. Bayern shows 657.5 Mio € for 43 players — clarify UX.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Kader tab renders expanded squads; Transfer club links clickable and navigate correctly)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Both new features verified. Real Madrid (20/1250M), Manchester City (18/1003M), Bayern (43/657.5M) confirmed via API + UI. TransferRow links work and navigation to /verein/<slug> confirmed. Minor unrelated: GET /api/transfers?player_id=<id> returns HTTP 500; the working endpoint is /api/players/{id}/transfers.
